title: Reconciler: refresh the integration branch from the base branch at run start (tracker records included)
description:
Found by the Phase 1 gate run: after epic cia completed (run gate-cia-2), two follow-up ticks were created on ticks main; a new run (gate-cia-3) read its tracker from the integration branch epic/cia, where those ticks do not exist, and refused with 'epic cia has no dispatchable tick' although tk graph on main lists both as ready. The integration branch's tracker diverges from the base branch the moment either side writes, and today nothing folds the base back in. At run start (and on every restart), before planning, the reconciler must refresh the integration branch from the epic's base branch as origin has it: a merge of origin/<base> into origin/<integration> performed with ticks' own merge drivers for tracker records — the manifest's exit-code drivers merge-file (.tick/issues) and merge-activity (.tick/activity), declared in the target repo's .gitattributes — committed with plumbing and pushed with the store's CAS discipline; a source-file conflict is a typed refusal (resolve-conflict role, Phase 2), never a silent skip. Read the base branch from the epic tick (base_branch field via tk show --json) and fall back to the run's --base. Tests: a fixture where a tick is created on main after the run's first wave is dispatched on the next run; a fixture where main and the integration branch both wrote .tick/activity merges cleanly through merge-activity; a source conflict refuses. Scope: internal/reconcile (+ internal/tk if the merge drivers need a helper — merge-file/merge-activity are manifest commands). Runs after 0x1 (same package).

## How this fits
Wave 7 of epic qeu, the last implementation tick before the final review. Integration commit 96eadde925c4b91dfe2d9304acacfd1cd4c0442a on epic/qeu includes 0x1 (records carry no host paths) and cgx (tracker writes in a detached worktree of the integration branch, internal/reconcile/tracker.go — the natural place for the base-branch fold). The gate run proved the workaround by hand: merging origin/main into epic/cia in a clone with merge.tick.driver='tk merge-file %O %A %B %P' and merge.tick-activity.driver='tk merge-activity %O %A %B %P' (from ticks' .gitattributes: .tick/issues/*.json merge=tick, .tick/activity/activity.jsonl merge=tick-activity) merged cleanly; note the drivers take FOUR args. No other worker is active. Stdlib only; verify your base: git merge-base --is-ancestor 96eadde925c4b91dfe2d9304acacfd1cd4c0442a HEAD.
